reviewer: Codex parent session; independent of the fixture-generation invocation

findings.bullet: - app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — The diff deletes `app/defaults.json` (previously `{"timeout":30}`), but `app/startup.py:6` still reads it unconditionally via `json.loads(Path(__file__).with_name("defaults.json").read_text())`, and nothing in the diff updates or removes that caller or repoints it at the new `load_config`. — Any call to `load_defaults()` now raises `FileNotFoundError`, so startup paths that read application defaults fail outright rather than falling back to the 30-second timeout.
findings.reason: Names the deleted defaults file, its unchanged load_defaults consumer, and FileNotFoundError on invocation; the base-side citation matches the deletion.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `is_valid_port` returns `0 < p < 65535`, which is exclusive at the top end and so returns `False` for `p = 65535`, the highest legal TCP port; the docstring on line 21 states the intended range is `1-65535`. — A service or client configured on port 65535 is rejected as invalid, and no test covers the upper boundary to catch it.
findings.reason: Identifies input 65535 and the exclusive upper bound, explaining rejection of a valid TCP port.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — `load_config` wraps the open and parse in `except Exception: return {}`, discarding the exception with no log, no caller signal, and no comment or docstring stating the fallback is intentional; a missing file, a permission error, and malformed JSON all produce the same `{}` as a genuinely empty config file. — A typo'd config path or a syntax error in the config silently starts the application on built-in defaults, and the operator has no message identifying which of the three failures occurred.
findings.reason: Names realistic file/JSON errors that become an indistinguishable empty configuration, with no caller diagnostic.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:38 — tests — The added trailing-dot branch (`if h.endswith("."): h = h[:-1]`) and the empty-string branch at line 36 are exercised by no test; the only added test, `tests/test_parse.py:17`, passes `"Example.COM"`, which takes neither branch. — A regression in the FQDN trailing-dot strip (for example `normalize_host("Example.COM.")`) or in the empty-string return would pass the suite undetected.
findings.reason: Identifies the untested trailing-dot branch and a concrete stripping regression that the existing lowercase-only test misses; credit is for that distinct branch.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:35 — comments — The docstring says `returns None when h is empty`, but the code at lines 36–37 is `if h == "": return ""`, returning an empty string, not `None`. — A caller trusting the docstring will guard with `if normalize_host(h) is None`, which never fires, so the empty-host case flows through as a valid empty hostname.
findings.reason: Contrasts the promised None with the actual empty-string result and explains how callers checking for None are misled.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:29 — tests — `load_config` has no test at all, so its success path (reading and parsing a real JSON file through `_fastjson.loads`) is unexercised by the suite. — The new public loader could be broken by a later refactor of the import fallback or the read with no failing test.
findings.reason: The valid-JSON success path also has no test; this is a separate regression risk from the swallowed-error defect and does not increase planted-defect recall.
